sentences.en: Back in 2011, a 13-year-old girl posted a music video on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 早在2011年，一个13岁的女孩在YouTube上发布了一段音乐视频。

sentences.en: It sat there for about a month without getting much notice.
sentences.zh: 它在那里放了大约一个月，没有引起太多关注。

sentences.en: But then, something totally unexpected happened.
sentences.zh: 但随后，发生了完全意想不到的事。

sentences.en: The girl's name was Rebecca Black, and the song she was singing in the video was called Friday.
sentences.zh: 女孩名叫丽贝卡·布莱克，她在视频中唱的歌名叫《星期五》。

sentences.en: More and more people started watching it, leaving comments, and sharing it.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人开始观看、留言并分享它。

sentences.en: Friday became the most-watched YouTube video of 2011, with 167 million views.
sentences.zh: 《星期五》成为2011年YouTube上观看次数最多的视频，播放量达到1.67亿次。

sentences.en: Plenty of people watched the video to make fun of it,
sentences.zh: 许多人观看这个视频是为了嘲笑它，

sentences.en: perhaps not knowing or caring that Rebecca Black was only 13 years old.
sentences.zh: 或许他们并不知道，也不在乎丽贝卡·布莱克当时只有13岁。

sentences.en: But a decade later, she's gotten the last laugh with a new remix of the song.
sentences.zh: 但十年后，她通过这首歌的一个新混音版本，笑到了最后。

sentences.en: with millions of views in the first few days after its release.
sentences.zh: 在发布后的头几天里就获得了数百万的浏览量。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, what makes certain songs, memes, and even social movements go viral?
sentences.zh: 本周的“隐藏的大脑”节目将探讨：是什么让某些歌曲、迷因，甚至是社会运动走红？

sentences.en: We'll look at why they spread, and how social contagion can be harnessed to build a better world.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨它们为什么会传播，以及如何利用社会传染来建设一个更好的世界。

sentences.en: How is it some social movements take off and spread, while others find themselves stuck?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些社会运动能够兴起并传播，而另一些却陷入停滞？

sentences.en: Why do some companies soar and become household names, while others flame out?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些公司能腾飞并家喻户晓，而另一些却昙花一现？

sentences.en: Can you predict success and failure, or is it all a matter of luck?
sentences.zh: 你能预测成功与失败，还是这全凭运气？

sentences.en: These are questions that have long fascinated Damon Santola.
sentences.zh: 这些问题长期以来一直深深吸引着达蒙·森托拉。

sentences.en: He's a sociologist at the University of Pennsylvania, and the author of the book, Change.
sentences.zh: 他是宾夕法尼亚大学的社会学家，也是《变革》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Damon Santola, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 达蒙·森托拉，欢迎来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I want to start with one model of how something can spread very, very rapidly.
sentences.zh: 我想从一个关于事物如何能非常、非常迅速地传播的模型开始谈起。

sentences.en: In late 2019, Damon, a few people got infected with the COVID-19 virus in Wuhan, the Chinese city.
sentences.zh: 2019年底，达蒙，中国武汉有几个人感染了新冠病毒。

sentences.en: Paint a picture for me of how a virus can go from infecting a small number of people in one Chinese city to a global pandemic.
sentences.zh: 请为我描绘一下，病毒是如何从中国一个城市的一小部分人感染发展成全球大流行的。

sentences.en: Yeah, the way that virus is typically spread is through social contact.
sentences.zh: 是的，病毒通常的传播方式是通过社会接触。

sentences.en: So that means that a few people in Wuhan will infect their friends and neighbors, the people they interact with directly.
sentences.zh: 这意味着武汉的一些人会传染给他们的朋友和邻居，也就是他们直接互动的人。

sentences.en: But it also means that if any one of those people gets onto an airplane and travels, say, to Tel Aviv or to Berlin,
sentences.zh: 但这同时也意味着，如果其中任何一个人登上一架飞机去旅行，比方说去特拉维夫或柏林，

sentences.en: then that infected person can infect the people around them on the airplane just by mere proximity.
sentences.zh: 那么这个被感染的人仅凭近距离接触，就能传染飞机上周围的人。

sentences.en: And then, obviously, those people, when they get off the plane, will infect their friends and neighbors and so forth.
sentences.zh: 然后，显而易见，这些人下飞机后会传染他们的朋友、邻居，以此类推。

sentences.en: And if those people get on an airplane, then, of course, this spreads to a new part of the world.
sentences.zh: 如果这些人再坐飞机，那么这自然就会传播到世界的新地区。

sentences.en: And so when we think about how this spreading process grows and how it spreads from one town to the globe,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们思考这种传播过程是如何增长的，以及它是如何从一个小镇蔓延到全球的时，

sentences.en: we really sort of can imagine it as a series of firework explosions where one infected community basically infects everyone that they come in contact with.
sentences.zh: 我们真的可以把它想象成一系列的烟花爆炸，其中一个受感染的社区基本上会传染与其接触的每个人。

sentences.en: And then all of those people become sort of the center of their own fireworks explosions.
sentences.zh: 然后所有这些人又都成为各自烟火爆炸的中心。

sentences.en: And what you get is this cascading series of fireworks that very quickly, through rapid communication and transportation networks, spread around the world.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的是这种层层递进的烟花级联反应，通过快速的通信和交通网络，它们在极短时间内传遍了世界各地。

sentences.en: So one of your central contentions is that the way people are connected to each other, their social networks, influence how things spread or how they fail to spread.
sentences.zh: 因此，你的核心论点之一是，人与人之间的连接方式、即他们的社会网络，影响了事物是如何传播的，或者是它们为什么未能传播。

sentences.en: But let's just drill down a second deeper.
sentences.zh: 但让我们再深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: Let's look at the social networks that allow a virus to spread exponentially.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看使病毒呈指数级传播的社会网络。

sentences.en: Let's say I'm at an airport.
We're sitting next to each other at a gate waiting for our flights.
sentences.zh: 我们并肩坐在登机口等待航班。

sentences.en: We don't talk to one another.
But this chance meeting allows a virus to leap between us.
sentences.zh: 但这种偶然的相遇使病毒得以在我们之间跃传。

sentences.en: So for this network, transmitting the virus requires very brief contact between us, almost like a glancing connection, right?
sentences.zh: 所以对于这个网络而言，传播病毒需要我们之间非常短暂的接触，有点像擦肩而过的连接，对吧？

sentences.en: And in many ways, we think about other kinds of contagions that way, too.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，我们对其他类型的传染病也是这么看的。

sentences.en: And we think about the spread of information.
sentences.zh: 我们也会这样看待信息的传播。

sentences.en: If you're sitting next to me at an airport and you tell me about a great new NPR show or a great new app that I can download, that I may do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你在机场坐在我旁边，告诉我一个很棒的新的NPR节目或一个我可以下载的绝佳新应用，我可能就会去下载。

sentences.en: And I can tell someone else that once I get home.
sentences.zh: 等我回到家后，我也可以告诉别人。

sentences.en: And that's exactly how diseases spread as well.
sentences.zh: 这正是疾病传播的方式。

sentences.en: And so we can think about this epidemiological model, the spread of diseases,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以将这种流行病学模型、即疾病的传播，

sentences.en: as a metaphor or as an underlying guide for thinking about all kinds of spreading processes and how just simple contact with a stranger can transmit really anything around the world.
sentences.zh: 作为思考各种传播过程的隐喻或潜在指南，看看与陌生人的简单接触是如何将任何东西传遍全世界的。

sentences.en: So it's very appealing to think that most things spread like viruses.
sentences.zh: 所以，认为大多数事物像病毒一样传播是非常吸引人的。

sentences.en: You know, so you have the example of the COVID-19 virus or a song like Friday, and it's easy to think that maybe everything spreads this way.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如新冠病毒或是像《星期五》这样的歌曲，人们很容易认为或许所有事物都是这样传播的。

sentences.en: Can you talk for a moment about how this fairly simple model of how things spread, how that model in some ways has, you know, if you will, gone viral?
sentences.zh: 你能聊聊这种相当简单的传播模型在某些方面是如何“走红”的吗？

sentences.en: So the notion of influencers, which are highly connected people that we're all familiar with on social media sites like Instagram and Facebook and Twitter.
sentences.zh: 这就是网红的概念，也就是我们在Instagram、Facebook和Twitter等社交媒体网站上都很熟悉的那些高连接度人群。

sentences.en: And we tend to think of these influencers as the key to spreading any kind of, you know, innovation idea or social change process.
sentences.zh: 我们往往认为这些网红是传播任何形式的创新想法或社会变革过程的关键。

sentences.en: And that comes from viral thinking, because if one person who interacts with a lot of other people gets COVID-19, then that person is going to be a super spreader for the virus.
sentences.zh: 这源于病毒式思维，因为如果一个与许多其他人互动的人感染了新冠病毒，那么这个人就会成为该病毒的超级传播者。

sentences.en: So this idea that a highly connected person can, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，高连接度的人可以，你知道的，

sentences.en: be very effective for spreading something to lots of other people and therefore kind of set off an epidemic all by themselves is an intuition that sits underneath viral marketing campaigns and the whole sort of influencer marketing approach.
sentences.zh: 在向许多其他人传播某事方面非常有效，从而能凭一己之力引发一场流行病，这种直觉正是病毒式营销活动和整个网红营销方法论的底层逻辑。

sentences.en: And so for nearly a century, actually, the assumption has been that everything spreads just like a virus does.
sentences.zh: 因此，实际上近一个世纪以来，人们一直假设所有事物的传播方式都和病毒一模一样。

sentences.en: And I feel like you hear this narrative very often in the news.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你在新闻中经常听到这种说法。

sentences.en: You cite the example of Oprah Winfrey sharing word in April 2009 about a new social media platform called Twitter.
sentences.zh: 你引用了奥普拉·温弗瑞在2009年4月透露一个名为Twitter的新社交媒体平台的例子。

sentences.en: Listen to this tape about that moment.
Hi, it's Friday Live and I'm on Twitter for the first time.
sentences.zh: 嗨，这里是“周五直播”，我第一次上Twitter。

sentences.en: Sitting next to me is Evan Williams, the co-founder of Twitter.
sentences.zh: 坐在我旁边的是Twitter的联合创始人埃文·威廉姆斯。

sentences.en: Can you believe all this Tweedly D stuff going on?
sentences.zh: 你能相信所有这些叽叽喳喳的玩意儿吗？

sentences.en: How did it come to life?
How did it come to life?
So, Damon, what is the conventional story of how Oprah's first tweet produced exponential growth of the Twitter platform?
sentences.zh: 那么，达蒙，奥普拉的第一条推文如何促成了Twitter平台的指数级增长，这个传统的故事是怎么说的？

sentences.en: It's exactly what you would imagine, which is Twitter wasn't growing very faSt.
sentences.zh: 这完全符合你的想象，也就是Twitter当时增长得并不快。

sentences.en: And then what we see in the timeline after and around Oprah's adoption of Twitter is that, you know, Twitter has, you know, by I think the end of that month, 28 million users.
sentences.zh: 然后我们在奥普拉开始使用Twitter之后及周围的时间线中看到的是，Twitter拥有了，我认为到那个月底，有2800万用户。

sentences.en: And so the natural thing to do or the kind of intuitive justification or rationale for what we see happening is to say, oh, they were, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以很自然会做出的事情，或者对我们所见现象的直观解释和理由就是：哦，他们，你知道的，

sentences.en: that company was successful in getting a, you know, a high profile influencer to endorse their product.
sentences.zh: 那家公司成功让一个知名网红来为其产品背书。

sentences.en: And as a result, their product was then adopted by a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们的产品随后被许多人采纳了。

sentences.en: So I want to spend a moment defining a couple of terms that are going to come up repeatedly in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 因此，我想花点时间定义几个在对话中会反复出现的术语。

sentences.en: Let's return to that moment in the airport.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到机场的那个时刻。

sentences.en: Sociologists call the connection that you and I had at the gate a weak tie.
sentences.zh: 社会学家把我和你在登机口建立的连接称为弱连结。

sentences.en: And can you give me some other examples of weak ties?
sentences.zh: 你能给我举几个弱连结的其他例子吗？

sentences.en: I should mention that the term weak ties and its complement, strong tie, come from the sociologist Mark Granovetter, who is personally one of my intellectual heroes.
sentences.zh: 我应该提到，弱连结这个词以及它的对立面强连结，都来自社会学家马克·格兰诺维特，他个人是我的学术偶像之一。

sentences.en: He defined these terms back in 1973.
sentences.zh: 他在1973年定义了这些术语。

sentences.en: Now, the glancing contact that happens in the airport, Mark Granovetter referred to as a weak tie.
sentences.zh: 现在，马克·格兰诺维特将发生在机场的这种擦肩而过的接触称为弱连结。

sentences.en: Because if you and I are sitting next to each other in an airport, we're not likely to know each other's friends or family.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你和我并肩坐在机场，我们不太可能认识彼此的朋友或家人。

sentences.en: We're not likely to even ever meet again.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可能再也不会见面。

sentences.en: Connection can act as an important, in some senses, like vital transmission point for a piece of information from your community to my community.
sentences.zh: 这种连接可以在某种意义上充当一个重要的、甚至是至关重要的传输点，将信息从你的社区传送到我的社区。

sentences.en: And so what Mark did that was so interesting is notice that these weak ties that don't play a huge role in how we conceptualize or think about our social networks are largely invisible.
sentences.zh: 马克所做的那件如此有趣的事情是，他注意到这些在我们的社交网络概念化或思考中不扮演重要角色的弱连结，在很大程度上是隐形的。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, they're playing this important role for the transmission of ideas and information and diseases, of course,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，它们在思想、信息以及疾病的传播中，扮演着将社区与社区、跨越国家、最终跨越世界联系起来的重要角色。

sentences.en: from community to community and across nations and ultimately across the world.
sentences.zh: 从社区到社区，跨越国家，并最终跨越整个世界。

sentences.en: So Mark Granovetter's influential paper was called The Strength of Weak Ties.
sentences.zh: 因此，马克·格兰诺维特具有影响力的论文名为《弱连结的力量》。

sentences.en: And besides being a very catchy title, it was about this very important idea that weak ties in some ways can spur things to travel very quickly and spread very faSt.
sentences.zh: 除了是一个非常吸引人的标题之外，它还探讨了这样一个极其重要的观点：弱连结在某些方面可以推动事物非常迅速地旅行和传播。

sentences.en: Can you give me some examples of the strength of weak ties in everyday life?
sentences.zh: 你能举一些日常生活中弱连结力量的例子吗？

sentences.en: Mark's actually initial example was looking at how people find out about jobs.
sentences.zh: 马克最初的例子实际上是关于人们如何找到工作的。

sentences.en: And, of course, when you're looking for a job and you're unemployed, you talk to your friends, you talk to your family,
sentences.zh: 当然，当你正在找工作且处于失业状态时，你会和朋友聊天，和家人聊天，

sentences.en: you sort of try to source out what available options there are in what you think of as your network.
sentences.zh: 你会试着在你认为的社交网络中寻找可用的机会。

sentences.en: But oftentimes, everyone in your community knows about the same openings because everyone in your community has the same friends and they know the same people.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，你社区里的每个人都知道同样的空缺职位，因为你社区里的每个人都有相同的朋友，他们认识同样的人。

sentences.en: And so it's very hard to learn about a new job opening or a new opportunity from the people that you already know.
sentences.zh: 因此，很难从你已经认识的人那里得知新的工作空缺或新的机会。

sentences.en: And so what Mark realized was that when people learn about new opportunities, it's often from these glancing contacts where you're just talking casually in the airport.
sentences.zh: 所以马克意识到，当人们了解到新的机会时，往往是通过那些擦肩而过的接触，比如你在机场随意聊天的时候。

sentences.en: And someone mentions, oh, I think that this division at Microsoft is hiring.
sentences.zh: 有人顺便提到，哦，我觉得微软的这个部门在招人。

sentences.en: Or I heard that actually there's a new Amazon's opening up a new branch in this area.
sentences.zh: 或者我听说亚马逊实际上正在这个地区开设新分部。

sentences.en: And that might be interesting to you that your friends and family might not know about.
sentences.zh: 这可能对你很有吸引力，而你的朋友和家人可能并不知道。

sentences.en: But that is, of course, incredibly relevant for you doing a job search.
sentences.zh: 但对你寻找工作而言，这当然是极其相关的。

sentences.en: And so these weak ties are incredibly effective and you can think of it as efficient for information transmission.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些弱连结极其有效，你可以认为它对信息传输而言是高效的。

sentences.en: You know, as new information comes up, it's very easy for that to spread across these sort of casual contacts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当新信息出现时，它很容易通过这些随意的接触传播开来。

sentences.en: You started to see evidence that this model of how things spread can have serious probleMs.
sentences.zh: 你开始看到证据表明，这种关于事物如何传播的模型可能存在严重问题。

sentences.en: And I want to point to a couple of moments of insight that you say that you had.
sentences.zh: 我想指出你曾提到过的几个灵光乍现的时刻。

sentences.en: You grew up in a Quaker community where you were part of a lot of marches for social justice.
sentences.zh: 你在贵格会社区长大，曾参加过许多争取社会正义的游行。

sentences.en: But you noticed that your classmates at school didn't always care about the same issues.
sentences.zh: 但你注意到，学校里的同学并不总是关心相同的问题。

sentences.en: How did this speak to the ability or the inability of weak ties to spread ideas?
sentences.zh: 这说明了弱连结传播思想的能力或无能，是怎么一回事？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, what I noticed was that across different groups or communities, it wasn't just they didn't care about them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我注意到的是，在不同的群体或社区中，并不仅仅是他们不关心。

sentences.en: They just didn't even know about them.
And if someone were to talk about an issue like water conservation or like fair gender practices in the workplace, at least in my middle school,
sentences.zh: 如果有人谈论像水资源保护或工作场所公平性别实践这样的话题，至少在我的初中里，

sentences.en: it wasn't something that people understood.
sentences.zh: 这不是人们能理解的事情。

sentences.en: And so you could announce that there's some march or rally or you could talk about the importance of these issues.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以宣布有某种游行或集会，或者你可以谈论这些问题的重要性。

sentences.en: largely fall on deaf ears because the community of classmates and the way that people talked about topics didn't really engage with or understand those ideas.
sentences.zh: 基本上会泥牛入海无人理睬，因为同学们所在的社区以及人们谈论主题的方式并没有真正参与或理解那些想法。

sentences.en: If everything spreads like a virus, how is it some ideas don't leap from group to group?
sentences.zh: 如果一切都像病毒一样传播，为什么有些思想没有在群体之间跃迁？

sentences.en: Damon was exposed to ideas about social justice at home.
sentences.zh: 达蒙在家里接触到了关于社会正义的思想。

sentences.en: So why didn't they leap through him to his classmates?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么它们没有通过他跃传给他的同学呢？

sentences.en: Why didn't he, if you will, infect them with those concepts?
sentences.zh: 为什么他没有，如果你愿意这么说的话，把那些概念“传染”给他们呢？
达蒙还注意到了另一件事。

sentences.en: Over time, some ideas that were popular in one community did spread to others.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，一些在一个社区中很受欢迎的想法确实传播到了其他社区。

sentences.en: But the way this happened did not look anything like a virus.
sentences.zh: 但发生这种现象的方式看起来一点也不像病毒。

sentences.en: Sometimes it took decades for those ideas to spread.
sentences.zh: 有时这些思想需要几十年的时间才能传播开来。

sentences.en: Take, for example, the support for renewable energy or gay rights.
sentences.zh: 以对可再生能源或同性恋权利的支持为例。

sentences.en: I noticed that some of those ideas actually had caught on by the time I started college.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，自我上大学时起，其中一些想法实际上就已经流行起来了。

sentences.en: A lot of people in the mainstream were talking about some of these issues in a sort of a regular, everyday way.
sentences.zh: 主流群体中的许多人正以一种常规的、日常生活的方式谈论其中的一些问题。

sentences.en: There were normal topics to think about.
sentences.zh: 这些都是很正常可以去思考的主题。

sentences.en: One of the most striking examples was like the organic foods movement,
sentences.zh: 最引人注目的例子之一就是有机食品运动，

sentences.en: which was a very marginal sort of fringe idea in the early 1980s that you would go to a grocery store and only buy, you know,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪80年代初，这是一个非常边缘的、非主流的想法，当时你要去杂货店只能买到，你知道的，

sentences.en: organic whole grain foods and have to go to a bulk bin to get it.
sentences.zh: 有机全谷物食品，还必须去散装货柜里买。

sentences.en: And a decade later, it was normal for grocery stores to have an aisle that was reserved for what they called health food.
sentences.zh: 十年后，杂货店里有一条专门留给他们所称的健康食品的过道，这已经是很正常的事了。

sentences.en: Then, of course, whole foods came along.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，全食超市（Whole Foods）出现了。

sentences.en: And so the influence of these peripheral movements on the mainstream was surprisingly effective for some things, but never landed for others.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些边缘运动对主流的影响在某些事情上出奇地有效，但对另一些事情却从不起作用。

sentences.en: Movements like water conservation, which was also a big one among some of the activists that I knew growing up, never really caught on in the mainstream of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 像水资源保护这样的运动，这也是我成长过程中认识的一些活动人士所关注的一大重点，在美国主流中从未真正流行起来，

sentences.en: And so the question that was raised for me, which I think is the really important question, is why?
sentences.zh: 因此对我来说产生了一个问题，我认为这也是真正重要的问题：为什么？

sentences.en: You know, is it just random or is there some underlying sort of scientific explanation for the success of some movements and the failure of others?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这只是随机的，还是说某些运动的成功和另一些的失败背后有着某种潜在的科学解释？

sentences.en: The Negro passengers on the city bus lines of Montgomery have been humiliated, intimidated and face threats on this bus line.
sentences.zh: 蒙哥马利市公交车上的黑人乘客一直受到羞辱、恐吓，并在这条公交线上面临威胁。

sentences.en: As a young scholar, you started to examine the growth and success of the civil rights movement, and you started to see problems with the conventional story of viral spread,
sentences.zh: 作为一名青年学者，你开始审视民权运动的发展与成功，你开始发现病毒式传播这一传统叙事存在的问题，

sentences.en: of how that movement took off.
sentences.zh: 即该运动是如何兴起的。

sentences.en: Can you describe that insight to me using the examples of Rosa Parks and a woman named Claudette Colvin?
sentences.zh: 你能用罗莎·帕克斯和一位名叫克劳黛特·科尔文的女性的例子来向我描述这一洞察吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the civil rights movement became one of the most interesting areas for me to study because of how the story is told.
sentences.zh: 是的，民权运动由于其故事的讲述方式，成为了我研究中最有趣的领域之一。

sentences.en: That with the Montgomery bus boycott, you know, Rosa Parks refused to move to the back of the bus, and she was arrested.
sentences.zh: 就像蒙哥马利公交车抵制运动一样，罗莎·帕克斯拒绝移到车厢后部，然后她被捕了。

sentences.en: And in many senses, this becomes a kind of galvanizing moment for the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这成了民权运动的一个催化剂时刻。

sentences.en: Just the other day, one of the fine citizens of our community, Mrs. Rosa Parks, was arrested because she refused to give up her seat for a white passenger.
sentences.zh: 就在前几天，我们社区的优秀公民罗莎·帕克斯太太被捕了，因为她拒绝给白人乘客让座。

sentences.en: And so the story that's told, which is analogous in many ways to kind of the sort of story of Twitter growing because of its moment on Oprah, the story that's told is there's,
sentences.zh: 因此流传着这样一个故事，它在很多方面类似于Twitter因奥普拉的节目而走红的故事，流传的故事是这样的：

sentences.en: you know, one person stands up and then, you know, a movement follows, and then the whole system of racial segregation collapses.
sentences.zh: 一个人站出来，然后一场运动随之兴起，接着种族隔离制度的整个体系就崩溃了。

sentences.en: But the truth of it is that, you know, lots and lots of women stood up intentionally against racial segregation on public buses.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，有许许多多的女性有意站出来反对公共汽车上的种族隔离。

sentences.en: Claudette Colvin is one of them, but there are dozens of others of women who, you know, took a stand against that racial injustice,
sentences.zh: 克劳黛特·科尔文就是其中之一，但还有几十名其他女性，她们站出来反对这种种族不公，

sentences.en: but they were arrested and nothing much came of it.
sentences.zh: 但她们被捕了，事情也没有什么实质性进展。

sentences.en: And I repeat, I told her I paid my fare and it's my constitutional right to sit here.
sentences.zh: 我再说一遍，我告诉过她我付了车费，坐在这里是我的宪法权利。

sentences.en: Claudette Colvin was 15 years old when she was arrested and dragged off a bus in handcuffs in Montgomery, Alabama.
sentences.zh: 克劳黛特·科尔文在阿拉巴马州蒙哥马利市被捕并被戴上手铐拖下公交车时年仅15岁。

sentences.en: This happened nine months before Rosa Parks did exactly the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这发生在罗莎·帕克斯做完全相同的事情的九个月前。

sentences.en: When the news reporters asked me, why didn't I get up?
sentences.zh: 当新闻记者问我，我为什么不起来？

sentences.en: I said, history had me glued to the seat.
sentences.zh: 我说，历史把我粘在座位上了。

sentences.en: I said, it felt as though, how are your tummy hands were pushing me down on one shoulder?
sentences.zh: 我说，感觉就像，你的肚子手在一边肩膀上把我往下压，

sentences.en: And so John O'Truth hand were pushing me down on another shoulder.
sentences.zh: 而约翰·奥·特鲁斯的手在另一边肩膀上把我往下压。

sentences.en: When we come back, how social networks explain the difference between the impact of Rosa Parks and the impact of Claudette Colvin.
sentences.zh: 广告回来后，我们将探讨社交网络如何解释罗莎·帕克斯的影响力与克劳黛特·科尔文的影响力之间的差异。

sentences.en: Damon Santola is a sociologist at the University of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 达蒙·森托拉是宾夕法尼亚大学的社会学家。

sentences.en: He studies how change unfolds within communities, within companies, within countries.
sentences.zh: 他研究变革如何在社区、公司和国家内部展开。

sentences.en: He argues that the conventional models we have about virality don't describe why one social movement takes off while a second stalls.
sentences.zh: 他认为，我们关于病毒式传播的传统模型无法解释为什么某个社会运动会腾飞，而另一个却停滞不前。

sentences.en: Damon, you draw a very important distinction in your book between what you call simple contagion and complex contagion.
sentences.zh: 达蒙，你在书中提出了一个非常重要的区别，即你所说的简单传染与复杂传染。

sentences.en: What do you mean by those terms?
sentences.zh: 你所说的这些术语是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, if we think of social change as a contagion process, some people accept an idea and then the people they come in contact with accept it and so forth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我们把社会变革视为一个传染过程，一些人接受了一个观点，然后与他们接触的人也接受了，以此类推。

sentences.en: It's natural to think of that in a viral way, spreading just like a virus would.
sentences.zh: 很自然地会从病毒传播的角度去思考，就像病毒传播一样。

sentences.en: And that is really the notion of simple contagion,
sentences.zh: 这确实就是简单传染的概念，

sentences.en: which is just about everyone that an infected or activated or excited person comes in contact with also becomes excited and activated.
sentences.zh: 即被感染、激活或兴奋的人接触到的几乎所有人也会变得兴奋和被激活。

sentences.en: I'm here to join the people bringing attention to Lou Gehrig's disease by taking the ALS ice bucket challenge.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是通过接受冰桶挑战，加入到引起人们对卢伽雷氏症关注的行列中来。

sentences.en: And so that's how a meme spreads or that's how a sort of contagious news story spreads from person to person.
sentences.zh: 这就是模因传播的方式，或者说是一种具传染性的新闻故事在人与人之间传播的方式。

sentences.en: And when we think about simple contagions, what we're really talking about is ideas that are familiar, products that we already really know,
sentences.zh: 当我们考虑简单传染时，我们真正讨论的是那些我们熟悉的想法、我们已经真正了解的产品，

sentences.en: things that make sense to us intuitively.
sentences.zh: 那些对我们来说凭直觉就能理解的事物。

sentences.en: And so when we see a new one, it's not a lot of work emotionally or cognitively or in any other way to just adopt it and pass it on.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们看到一个新事物时，在情感上、认知上或其他任何方面，采纳并传递它都不需要费太多功夫。

sentences.en: Complex contagions, by contrast, are the kinds of social change initiatives or the kinds of ideas or the kinds of products that we resist initially, that aren't familiar,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，复杂传染是我们最初会抵触的、不熟悉的、诡异的或有点与众不同的社会变革倡议、想法或产品。

sentences.en: that are weird or a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 仅仅接触一个倡导它或已经采纳它的人，并不足以说服我们也这样做。

sentences.en: Just coming into contact with one person who's advocating for it or who has adopted it isn't enough to convince us that we should do it too.
sentences.zh: 这方面的一个很好的例子就像是，你知道的，参加抗议游行，你可能会参加抗议游行，因为这是一个好主意，而且你支持这项运动。

sentences.en: A great example of this is something like, you know, joining a protest march, where you might join a protest march because it's a good idea and you're on board with the movement.
sentences.zh: 但如果你对这项运动一无所知，你根本不了解它。

sentences.en: But if you have no idea about the movement, you're not oriented to it at all.
You don't really care about it.
sentences.zh: 如果存在被捕的可能性或警察报复的可能性，这种选择就会伴随着一定的风险。

sentences.en: And if there's the possibility of being arrested or the possibility of police retaliation, there's some risk involved with that choice.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅仅因为你认识的人在这么做，并不意味着你就会确信自己也应该这么做。

sentences.en: And so just because someone you know is doing it doesn't mean you're going to be convinced that you should do it too.
sentences.zh: 这就是简单传染和复杂传染之间的巨大区别。

sentences.en: And this is the sort of the big difference between a simple contagion and a complex contagion.
sentences.zh: 对于简单传染的传播，只需与一个人接触就够了。

sentences.en: For a simple contagion to spread, all it takes is contact with one person.
sentences.zh: 你基本上只是发现了它。

sentences.en: You're just basically finding out about it.
sentences.zh: 你发现了这个新模因，然后你可以观看并传播它。

sentences.en: You found out about the new meme and you can watch it and spread it.
sentences.zh: 但对于复杂传染，你需要被说服。

sentences.en: But for a complex contagion, you need to be convinced.
sentences.zh: 复杂传染的标志之一是它们需要人们承担一定的成本。

sentences.en: One of the hallmarks of complex contagions is they require people to accept certain costs.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让人们以某种重要的方式改变他们的行为，你想让他们更多地回收利用、更慢地开车或实践安全性行为，

sentences.en: If you want people to change their behavior in some important way, you want them to recycle more or drive more slowly or practice safe sex,
sentences.zh: 这些改变可能会涉及个人成本。

sentences.en: these changes can involve personal costs.
sentences.zh: 它们不像分享某人做冰桶挑战的视频或转发《星期五》之歌那样成本几乎为零。

sentences.en: They're not like sharing a video of someone doing the ice bucket challenge or passing on the Friday song, which has almost zero costs.
sentences.zh: 为什么促使人们分享猫咪视频的社交网络，会与能让某人走上街头抗议种族不公的社交网络不同呢？

sentences.en: Why would it be that the social networks that prompt people to share cat videos are different from the social networks that can get someone out on the street to protest racial injustice?
sentences.zh: 为了解释这一点，达蒙引用了2013年的一個例子，当时人权运动在Facebook上发起了一项倡议，以建立对同性婚姻的支持。

sentences.en: To explain, Damon cites an example from 2013, when the human rights campaign launched an initiative on Facebook to build support for same-sex marriage.
sentences.zh: 因为最高法院当时正在审理这起关于同性婚姻的案件。

sentences.en: Because the Supreme Court was hearing this case about same-sex marriage.
sentences.zh: 该倡议是让人们将他们的个人资料照片更改为粉红色和红色的等号，以表示对该运动的支持。

sentences.en: And the initiative was to have people change their profile photo to an equal sign that was pink and red to show support for the movement.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始浏览我的动态，简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: And then I started looking through my feed and I just couldn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 字面意思就是红色的符号一遍又一遍地出现。

sentences.en: It was literally just a red symbol over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 大约24小时后，我们就知道我们确实搞出了一些病毒式传播的东西。

sentences.en: It was about 24 hours when we knew that we were really on to something that had gone viral.
sentences.zh: 现在，这项倡议在不到一周的时间里传播给了近300万Facebook用户。

sentences.en: Now, this initiative spread to almost 3 million Facebook users in under a week.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是病毒式传播的东西。

sentences.en: So that sounds like something that's viral.
sentences.zh: 但一些数据科学家和物理学家更仔细地研究了这些数据。

sentences.en: But some data scientists and physicists looked more closely at the data.
sentences.zh: 他们看到的是，这种社会传染的传播，这种支持同性婚姻的变革倡议的传播，

sentences.en: And what they saw was that the spreading of this social contagion, this sort of change initiative to support same-sex marriage,
sentences.zh: 是一种复杂传染，尽管它的传播速度非常快。

sentences.en: was a complex contagion, even though it spread really faSt.
sentences.zh: 这种复杂传染的特征是，在人们从其中一个邻居那里采纳它之前，

sentences.en: And the signature of this complex contagion was that before people adopted it from one of their neighbors,
sentences.zh: 他们会等待更多的邻居采纳它。

sentences.en: they waited for more of their neighbors to adopt it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想你在Facebook上的生活，你会与许多不同的人建立连接。

sentences.en: And if you think about your life on Facebook, you're connected to lots of different people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可能会看到你的祖父母，你可能与你的父母有连接，

sentences.en: You know, you may see your grandparents, you may be connected to your parents,
sentences.zh: 你的大学朋友，你的高中朋友，你工作认识的人，你社区的人。

sentences.en: your friends from college, your friends from high school, people you know from work, people from your neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人都在某种程度上评估你的行为。

sentences.en: And all of those people are sort of evaluating your behavior.
sentences.zh: 因此，采纳某种带有争议性的事物会存在某种社会风险，

sentences.en: So there's some sort of social risk on adopting something that's kind of controversial
sentences.zh: 或者可能不被这些人接受。

sentences.en: or may not be accepted by these people.
sentences.zh: 或者你甚至可能会冒着在你的社交媒体网站上引发口水战或争论的风险。

sentences.en: Or you may even run the risk of starting a flame war, an argument on your social media site.
sentences.zh: 人们所做的是，他们等到两三个、四五个类似联系人采纳了之后才行动。

sentences.en: What people did is they waited until two, three, four, five of their sort of contacts adopted.
sentences.zh: 然后这给了他们足够的信心，让他们确信这种新行为是合法的，然后他们也会采纳。

sentences.en: And then that gave them enough confidence that this new behavior was legitimate and then they would adopt too.
sentences.zh: 现在，你需要来自几个人的社会强化来说服你采纳某事这个想法，

sentences.en: Now, that idea that you need social reinforcement from several people to convince you to adopt something
sentences.zh: 意味着你需要能够产生某种来自同伴的强化压力的网络。

sentences.en: means that you need networks that create a kind of, you know, reinforcing pressure from peers.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回想一下新冠病毒的传播，它的传播就像烟花爆炸一样。

sentences.en: If we remember when we think about the spread of the coronavirus, it spread like a fireworks explosion.
sentences.zh: 所以一个人采纳并感染了很多人。

sentences.en: So one person adopted and infected lots of people.
sentences.zh: 然后这些人，你知道的，又感染了许多其他人，而最初的那个人可能并不认识他们，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then those people, you know, infected lots of other people that the first person may not know and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 因此，烟花爆炸并没有太多的冗余度。

sentences.en: And so a fireworks explosion doesn't have a lot of redundancy in it.
It's got a ton of reach.
sentences.zh: 因此它可以非常快地传遍全球。

sentences.en: And so it can get across the world really faSt.
sentences.zh: 但它没有那种来自人们采纳并相互分享一个观点、从而为之创造大量强化的社会说服力。

sentences.en: But it doesn't have a lot of that kind of social convincement from people adopting and kind of sharing one idea with each other and creating a lot of reinforcement for it.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上在这里触及了几个非常重要的不同想法，我们实际上应该慢慢地剖析它们，达蒙。

sentences.en: So you've actually touched on several different ideas here that are really important that we should actually unpack somewhat slowly, Damon.

sentences.zh: 你知道的，你书的核心是一个非常重要的见解。

sentences.en: You know, at the core of your book is a very important insight.
sentences.zh: 人们以任何重要方式改变行为的核心原因，是因为他们看到周围的人在改变他们的行为。

sentences.en: The central reason people change their behavior in any important way is because they see the people around them changing their behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以心理学家有时称之为社会证明。

sentences.en: So psychologists sometimes call this social proof.
sentences.zh: 我上Facebook是因为其他人也在上Facebook。

sentences.en: I get on Facebook because other people are on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我在街头游行，是因为我看到像我这样的人也在街头游行。

sentences.en: I march on the streets because I see other people like me marching on the streets.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这个见解应用到变革科学中，真正要问的问题可能不是我如何让这个人改变，

sentences.en: If you apply that insight to the science of change, the real question to ask might not be how do I make this person change,
sentences.zh: 而是我如何向这个人展示他们周围的人正在改变？

sentences.en: but how can I show this person that the people around them are changing?
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这难道不是真正试图推动这种复杂传染的人的目标吗？

sentences.en: Is that in some ways the goal of the person who's actually trying to drive this kind of complex contagion?

sentences.zh: 一个当然是让新的采纳者对这个想法感到兴奋。

sentences.en: One is, of course, to have new adopters get excited about the idea.
sentences.zh: 实现这一目标的一种方法是让他们的几个同伴和联系人采纳，

sentences.en: And one way to do that is to have several of their peers and contacts adopt,
sentences.zh: 这为该想法创造了信誉，使其看起来更被他们的朋友圈接受，并且还能对加入产生情感上的兴奋感。

sentences.en: which creates credibility for the idea and makes it seem more accepted by their friendship group and can also generate emotional excitement about getting on board.
sentences.zh: 但还有第二个部分，那就是如果这个想法相当具争议性，早期采纳的人如果发现没有其他人采纳，最终可能会放弃。

sentences.en: But there's a second part, which is that if the idea is fairly contentious, people who adopt early on, if they see that no one else has adopted, may wind up giving it up.
sentences.zh: 他们最终可能会说，嗯，我参与这事其实不是件好事，因为没有其他人支持它。

sentences.en: They may wind up saying, well, this is actually not a good thing for me to be a part of because no one else is supporting it.
sentences.zh: 因此，与现有采纳者以及展示对某个想法支持的人保持联系，可以让人们保持投入，并且它维持了对该想法的参与度。

sentences.en: And so having connections to existing adopters and to people who are showing support for an idea keeps people engaged and it sort of sustains membership in the idea.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你仔细想想，它其实更像是一个渔网，而不是一场烟花表演。

sentences.en: So if you think about it, it's really more like a fishing net than a fireworks display.
sentences.zh: 所以在渔网中，你有很多三角形将这些不同的社区和人连接起来，你知道的，

sentences.en: And so in a fishing net, you've got lots of triangles connecting these different neighborhoods and people, you know,
sentences.zh: 人们认识人，他们认识朋友的朋友，以此类推。

sentences.en: know people and they know their friends of friends and so forth.
sentences.zh: 这种冗余度让人们确信这个想法是值得的，

sentences.en: And that redundancy gives people confidence that the idea is worthwhile,
sentences.zh: 这种新行为是被接受的，然后使他们能够与其他新的采纳者协调，进而说服其他人采纳，以此类推。

sentences.en: that this new behavior is accepted and then allows them to coordinate with other new adopters to then convince other people to adopt and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 所以你做了一个有趣的实验，测试了冗余度在推动行为方面的力量。

sentences.en: So you ran an interesting experiment that sort of tested the power of redundancy in driving behavior.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它有点像是在比较烟花形状的网络中会发生什么，你知道的，我与三个人交谈，

sentences.en: In some ways, it sort of compared what happens in a network that is in the shape of fireworks where, you know, I'm talking to three people,
sentences.zh: 这三个人与另外三个人交谈，以此类推；而渔网的例子则是，你知道的，我在一个网络中与其他所有人连接。

sentences.en: those three people are talking to three other people and so on versus a fishing net example where, you know, I'm connected in a network with other people.
sentences.zh: 并且我不断地从网络中的同一些人那里一遍又一遍地听到声音。

sentences.en: And I'm constantly hearing from the same people in the network over and over again.
sentences.zh: 你做了一个实验，试图通过这两种不同的社交网络来推动一项健康干预措施。

sentences.en: You ran an experiment trying to drive a health intervention looking at these two different kinds of social networks.
sentences.zh: 关于冗余度与实际让人们改变行为的有效性之间的关系，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: What did you find about the relationship between redundancy and the effectiveness of actually getting people to change their behavior?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我做的是创造了一个包含大约150人的烟花爆炸网络，然后是一个拥有相同人数的类似网络。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, what I did is created a fireworks explosion network with about 150 people in it and then a similar network with the same number of people.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都连接在一个渔网中。

sentences.en: But everyone was connected into a fishing net.
sentences.zh: 每个人都被，你知道的，给予机会去知道他们将了解一种新的健康技术。

sentences.en: And everyone was, you know, given the opportunity to know that they would learn about a new health technology.
sentences.zh: 然后我把这种健康技术与每个网络中的一个人放在一起，接着只想看看这些联系人中究竟有谁会去注册那种新的健康技术。

sentences.en: And then I put the health technology with one person into each network and then wanted to just see if which of those contacts would go sign up for that new health technology.
sentences.zh: 哪个社交网络会引发行为改变？

sentences.en: Which social network would trigger behavioral change?
sentences.zh: 是组织得像烟花表演那样、人们在不断扩展的链条中与其他人的网络？

sentences.en: The one organized like a fireworks display where people are connected to others in an expanding chain?
sentences.zh: 还是渔网那样，人们在一个闭环中连接？

sentences.en: Or the fishing net, where people were connected in a closed loop?
sentences.zh: 达蒙发现，尽管信息在组织得像渔网一样的网络中传播得较慢，但该网络中实际上有更多的人改变了他们的行为。

sentences.en: Damon found that although information spread more slowly in the network organized like a fishing net, more people in that network actually changed their behavior.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为尽管在信息信号方面传遍网络需要稍长一点的时间，

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that although it took a little bit longer to reach around the network in terms of the informational signal,
sentences.zh: 但采纳的实际增长在这些渔网网络中的传播速度比在烟花网络中要快得多、远得多。

sentences.en: the actual growth of adoption spread much faster and much farther across these fishing net networks than across the firework network.
sentences.zh: 现在，我把这个相同的实验做了六次，得到了相同的结果，这意味着，你知道的，你可以得出非常强有力的结论，

sentences.en: Now, I ran this same experiment six different times and I got the same result, which means, you know, you can draw a very powerful kind of conclusion,
sentences.zh: 也就是你可以做出一个强有力的科学主张，即通过在一群网民之间构建一个通信网络，

sentences.en: which is you can make a strong scientific claim that by structuring a communication network among a group of people online,
sentences.zh: 你可以改变人们采纳新行为的可能性。

sentences.en: you can change people's likelihood of adopting a new behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以退一步从宏观角度来看，我们最初讨论的是病毒以及病毒是如何传播的。

sentences.en: So just to step back and look at the big picture for a second, we started by talking about viruses and how viruses spread.
sentences.zh: 我们表明病毒是通过这种弱联系网络传播的。

sentences.en: And we showed that viruses spread through this network of weak ties.
sentences.zh: 人们只是略微认识彼此。
他们有这种泛泛的接触。
非常迅速地，某种东西就能从中国的一个城市传遍整个地球。

sentences.en: Very quickly, something can go from a city in China to all the way around the planet.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看了另一种改变，它涉及更困难得多的行为改变，

sentences.en: And then we looked at this other kind of change, which involves much more difficult, you know, behavioral change,
sentences.zh: 人们实际上必须以某种重要的方式改变他们的行为、态度或规范。

sentences.en: where people actually have to change their behavior or their attitudes or their norms in some important way.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他们通常需要强化，不仅来自一个人，而是来自多个与他们联系更紧密的人，也就是所谓的强联系网络。

sentences.en: And in order to do this, they often need reinforcement, not just from one, but from multiple people who are connected to them more closely, sort of a network of strong ties.
sentences.zh: 你提出这样的观点：对于复杂传染，也就是我们在谈论改变时大多数人实际在谈论的那种改变，

sentences.en: And you make the case that for complex contagion, which is actually the kind of change that most of us are actually talking about when we talk about change,
sentences.zh: 你实际上需要这些强联系，而不是弱联系网络。

sentences.en: you actually need these strong ties rather than the network of weak ties.
sentences.zh: 当你审视诸如民权运动之类的事物时，你发现人们是通过弱联系还是通过强联系改变他们的行为？

sentences.en: When you looked at something like the civil rights movement, did you find that people change their behavior through weak ties or through strong ties?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是关于民权运动最引人注目的发现之一，即证据完全支持强联系。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was one of the most striking findings about the civil rights movement is that the evidence all works in favor of strong ties.
sentences.zh: 这在当时是一个启示，因为先前的理论都认为，社会变革，特别是民权运动，

sentences.en: And that was a revelation at the time, because the theories had all said that, you know, social change, and in particular the civil rights movement,
sentences.zh: 可以用社交网络中的弱联系来解释，这些弱联系可以让关于活动的活动信息广泛传播。

sentences.en: would be explained by weak ties in social networks that would allow, you know, information about activities to spread far and wide.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，尽管信息广泛传播，但实际参与却没有。

sentences.en: But it turned out that although the information spread far and wide, actual participation didn't.
sentences.zh: 参与是通过聚集成群的朋友的朋友传播的，他们可以提供社会强化，降低参与风险，

sentences.en: Participation spread through, you know, friends of friends who are clustered together, who could provide social reinforcement, who could reduce the risk of participation,
sentences.zh: 并最终能够在新的参与者中产生强烈的传染性情感，

sentences.en: and ultimately could generate, you know,
sentences.zh: 使一场运动从网络边缘的集群发展到遍及全国。

sentences.en: a strong emotional contagion among new participants and grow a movement from a cluster in the periphery of the network to reach across the nation.
sentences.zh: 现在，所有这些在某种程度上制造了一个谜题，达蒙。

sentences.en: Now, all of this in some ways produces a puzzle, Damon.
sentences.zh: 如果人们希望看到别人改变自己才改变，合理的问题是，事情怎么会发生改变？

sentences.en: If people want to see others change before they change, the reasonable question is, how does anything ever change?
sentences.zh: 因为是什么让事情开始运转的？

sentences.en: Because what gets the ball rolling?
sentences.zh: 所以有些人可能会说，好吧，这就是名人和意见领袖发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: So some people might say, OK, that's where the celebrity or the influencer comes in.
sentences.zh: 这也是奥普拉发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: And that's where Oprah comes in.
sentences.zh: 如果某个名人公开支持某事，其他人就会效仿。

sentences.en: If a celebrity comes out in favor of something, others will follow.
sentences.zh: 你在很多方面称之为一个神话。

sentences.en: You call this a myth in many ways.
Why are celebrities not very effective at sparking behavioral change?
sentences.zh: 为什么名人对于激发行为改变并不是很有效？

sentences.en: Not just, it might be effective at sparking awareness, but why are they not very effective at sparking this kind of complex contagion?
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是，他们可能在激发认知方面很有效，但为什么他们在激发这种复杂的传染时效果不佳呢？

sentences.en: Well, there are two things you need to think about when you're dealing with what we refer to as influencers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你处理我们所说的“有影响力的人”时，有两件事你需要考虑。

sentences.en: And one is that what makes influencers so effective for spreading simple contagions is they've got lots and lots of ties.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是，使有影响力的人在传播简单传染方面如此高效的原因是，他们拥有非常非常多的社会联系。

sentences.en: But when it comes to complex contagions, again, ideas that are unfamiliar or ideas that maybe go against existing norms, the social influencer is highly observed.
sentences.zh: 但当涉及到复杂传染时——同样，那些不熟悉的想法，或者可能违背现有规范的想法——社会影响力人物受到的关注度很高。

sentences.en: A lot of people are paying attention to their behavior, which means they're fairly careful about deciding what they're going to do and not do.
sentences.zh: 很多人都在关注他们的行为，这意味着他们在决定做什么和不做什么时相当谨慎。

sentences.en: Someone doesn't become highly connected by ignoring their social ties.
sentences.zh: 没有人会通过忽视其社会联系而变得高度互联。

sentences.en: They become highly connected by paying a lot of attention to what people expect of them.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以变得高度互联，是因为他们非常关注人们对他们的期望。

sentences.en: And this is true in entertainment.
And so what that means is that when people are evaluating which new ideas to take on, which new products to adopt, particularly products that are public,
sentences.zh: 因此，这意味着当人们在评估要接受哪些新想法、采纳哪些新产品时，特别是那些公开的产品，

sentences.en: they have to take into account how everyone around them is going to sort of perceive that decision, which means that when it comes to complex contagions,
sentences.zh: 他们必须考虑到周围每个人将如何看待这个决定，这意味着在涉及复杂传染时，

sentences.en: all of the non-adopters are actually forces against adoption.
sentences.zh: 所有非采纳者实际上都是反对采纳的力量。
这是一个至关重要的想法。

sentences.en: Remember how we said the central goal in behavior change is to show people that those around them are changing?
sentences.zh: 还记得我们说过行为改变的核心目标是向人们展示周围的人正在改变吗？

sentences.en: Turns out the same thing goes for celebrities and influencers.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，名人 Influencer 也是如此。

sentences.en: They wait to see what their fans think.
sentences.zh: 他们等着看粉丝们的想法。

sentences.en: It may be counterintuitive, but if they don't see those people changing, they are hesitant to go firSt.
sentences.zh: 这可能与直觉相反，但如果他们没有看到这些人做出改变，他们就会犹豫着不敢率先行动。

sentences.en: And so this makes highly connected influencers into, you know, in some cases, a kind of a roadblock.
sentences.zh: 因此，这使得高度互联的 Influencer 在某些情况下变成了一种绊脚石。

sentences.en: And you see that most of the successful initiatives for social change, and this includes novel technologies like Twitter and Facebook,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，大多数成功的社会变革倡议（这包括 Twitter 和 Facebook 等新兴技术，

sentences.en: but it also includes social movements like Black Lives Matter, Arab Spring, and the Social Rights Movement,
sentences.zh: 但也包括 Black Lives Matter、阿拉伯之春和民权运动等社会运动），

sentences.en: grew from clusters of people in the network periphery who kind of grew a critical mass,
sentences.zh: 都成长于网络边缘的人群集群，他们逐渐形成了关键多数，

sentences.en: and also they had enough support that they went up tipping the center of the network, and then it spread to everyone.
sentences.zh: 而且他们拥有足够的支持，最终撼动了网络的中心，然后传播给了所有人。

sentences.en: But the origin story is always in the periphery, not in the center.
sentences.zh: 但起源故事总是发生在边缘，而不是中心。

sentences.en: You can see the same thing in the rise of former President Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 在前总统唐纳德·特朗普的崛起中，你也能看到同样的情况。

sentences.en: When he first announced his candidacy for president back in 2015, most people in the Republican establishment laughed him off.
sentences.zh: 早在 2015 年他首次宣布竞选总统时，共和党建制派的大多数人都对他的嘲笑置之不理。

sentences.en: Some media organizations declined to cover his campaign because they thought it was a joke.
sentences.zh: 一些媒体机构拒绝报道他的竞选活动，因为他们认为这是一个笑话。

sentences.en: But Trump caught on with people in the periphery of the Republican Party,
sentences.zh: 但特朗普吸引了共和党边缘地区的人们，

sentences.en: and gradually, his growing support from the margins overwhelmed the resistance of the establishment.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，来自边缘地区日益增长的支持压倒了建制派的阻力。

sentences.en: The change did not start from the center and move out.
sentences.zh: 这种改变并不是从中心开始并向外扩散的。

sentences.en: It started from the outside and moved in.
sentences.zh: 它是从外部开始并向内推进的。

sentences.en: Damon says the exact same thing happens outside the political sphere.
sentences.zh: 达蒙表示，在政治领域之外，完全相同的事情也在发生。

sentences.en: Take the example of something we talked about earlier, the rise of Twitter.
sentences.zh: 以我们之前谈论过的事物为例——Twitter 的崛起。

sentences.en: Yeah, the origin story of Twitter is quite interesting because it is a story of peripheral growth,
sentences.zh: 是的，Twitter 的起源故事相当有趣，因为它是一个边缘增长的故事，

sentences.en: but it's also a story, surprisingly, of neighborhood growth,
sentences.zh: 但出人意料的是，它也是一个邻里增长的故事，

sentences.en: which, when you think about internet technologies and social media,
sentences.zh: 当你想到互联网技术和社交媒体时，

sentences.en: it's almost a truism that they would spread, you know, in the ether
sentences.zh: 它们会在网络空间中传播，

sentences.en: and not be constrained at all by, like, local neighborhood geography.
sentences.zh: 并且根本不会受到诸如本地邻里地理等因素的限制，这几乎是一个老生常谈的真理。

sentences.en: But, in fact, Twitter grew initially in the San Francisco Bay Area
sentences.zh: 但事实上，Twitter 最初是在旧金山湾区发展起来的，

sentences.en: just through sort of friends and neighbors adopting from each other.
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过朋友和邻居之间互相采纳。

sentences.en: And so that's sort of the strong tie, complex contagion story,
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像强联系、复杂传染的故事，

sentences.en: but it gets more interesting because what ultimately happens is that there's an earthquake one day,
sentences.zh: 但它变得更有趣了，因为最终发生的事情是，有一天发生了一场地震，

sentences.en: and all of a sudden, it's not a big earthquake for the Bay Area,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，对湾区来说这不是一场大地震，
但不管怎样，它是一场地震。

sentences.en: And Twitter became very, very useful instantly because people could coordinate with one another
sentences.zh: Twitter 变得非常非常有用，因为人们可以相互协调，

sentences.en: to figure out, you know, where shocks and aftershocks were hitting,
sentences.zh: 弄清楚，你知道，冲击和余震发生在哪里，

sentences.en: what their expectations were for what to do, and where family members were and how they were handling it.
sentences.zh: 他们对该做什么的期望是什么，以及家庭成员在哪里以及他们是如何应对的。

sentences.en: And so the sort of network really kind of galvanized.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种网络真正地被激活了。

sentences.en: And then what happened that's pretty striking, I think, that's most surprising,
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件非常引人注目、我认为最令人惊讶的事情，

sentences.en: is that Twitter, once it caught hold in San Francisco, didn't jump to L.A.
sentences.zh: 那就是 Twitter 一旦在旧金山站稳脚跟，并没有跳到洛杉矶、

sentences.en: It actually started to spread across the countryside of California.
sentences.zh: 它实际上开始在加利福尼亚州的乡村地区传播。

sentences.en: It started to spread kind of south to San Jose and sort of north to Marin
sentences.zh: 它开始向南传播到圣何塞，向北传播到马林，

sentences.en: and to sort of slowly east to other parts of the sort of Bay Area and surrounding communities.
sentences.zh: 并缓慢向东传播到湾区其他地区及周边社区。

sentences.en: And what you saw was that, like, as Twitter grew, it wasn't spreading virally through networks online.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的是，随着 Twitter 的发展，它并不是通过网上的网络进行病毒式传播的。

sentences.en: It was spreading spatially through neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 它是通过社区进行空间传播的。

sentences.en: And then something really unexpected happened, which is that as it filled out around the Bay Area,
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件非常意想不到的事情，那就是随着它在湾区周围填满，

sentences.en: then Twitter showed up, again, not in New York or L.A., but it showed up in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: Twitter 又出现了——不是在纽约或洛杉矶，而是在马萨诸塞州剑桥市。

sentences.en: And that's where it sort of next took hold.
sentences.zh: 这就是它接下来站稳脚跟的地方。

sentences.en: And the reason is because a lot of people who live in San Francisco and Cambridge went to school together.
sentences.zh: 原因是因为许多住在旧金山和剑桥的人曾一起上学。

sentences.en: And they work in these different sectors, either along Route 28, 128 in Boston, which is a major technology area,
sentences.zh: 他们在这些不同的行业工作，要么沿着波士顿的 28 号、128 号公路（这是一个主要的技术区），

sentences.en: or along, you know, in Silicon Valley.
And so these two areas wind up being, like, highly connected socially with lots of reinforcing ties across them
sentences.zh: 因此，这两个地区最终在社交上高度互联，彼此之间有着大量强化联系，

sentences.en: and essentially form a network that's like a fishing net going from one part of the country to another.
sentences.zh: 本质上形成了一个像从国家一部分延伸到另一部分的捕鱼网一样的网络。

sentences.en: And then once it landed in Cambridge, it spread out again locally in Boston, around the Boston area.
sentences.zh: 一旦它在剑桥登陆，它就在波士顿本地、波士顿地区再次扩散。

sentences.en: And then when it sort of amplified and took off and jumped from Cambridge, Massachusetts to Seattle,
sentences.zh: 然后，当它被放大并腾飞，从马萨诸塞州剑桥跳到西雅图时，

sentences.en: which is another high-tech hub where people were connected to the other people and so forth
sentences.zh: 那是另一个高科技中心，那里的人们与其他人相连，诸如此类，

sentences.en: and sort of gained traction in more and more cities,
sentences.zh: 并在越来越多的城市获得关注，

sentences.en: then ultimately it reached a tipping point around January 2009.
sentences.zh: 最终在 2009 年 1 月左右达到了一个临界点。

sentences.en: And once it hit that tipping point, it just took off with hyper-exponential growth month after month.
sentences.zh: 一旦它达到了那个临界点，它就以月复一月的超指数增长腾飞了。

sentences.en: It went from, you know, $8 million to $20 million to $28 million very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 它非常非常快地从 800 万美元增长到 2000 万美元再到 2800 万美元。

sentences.en: And that's the point at which Oprah adopted was, you know, during that period of, like, massive growth.
sentences.zh: 这就是奥普拉采纳的时间点，你知道的，是在那段大规模增长的时期。

sentences.en: And even after that period, it continued to grow, but didn't grow as faSt.
sentences.zh: 即使在那段时期之后，它仍在继续增长，但增长没有那么快了。

sentences.en: Like, that was the window for Twitter's, you know, major explosion.
sentences.zh: 就像，那是 Twitter 主要爆发的窗口期。

sentences.en: And so Oprah is sort of at the tail end of that process, not at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以奥普拉可以说是处于这个过程的尾端，而不是开始。
